artists.biography: Haken (/ˈheɪkən/) are an English progressive metal band formed in 2007 by multi-instrumentalist Richard Henshall, guitarist Matthew Marshall, and vocalist Ross Jennings. While Henshall, Marshall, and Jennings first had the idea of forming Haken in 2004, they opted to pursue their instruments and songwriting first. Upon recruiting other members three years later, they eventually released the demo Enter the 5th Dimension in 2008, signing with Sensory Records and releasing their first album Aquarius in 2010. As of 2020, they have released six studio albums, an EP, and two live albums.

perplexity.description:
Haken's Affinity, released in 2016 on Inside Out Music, is the British progressive metal band's fourth studio album. Marking the first full-length appearance of bassist Conner Green, Affinity stands out for its distinct 1980s-inspired sound, blending classic progressive rock and metal with modern djent, post-rock, and ambient elements. The album's retro aesthetic is evident in both its cover art and musical references, with tracks like "1985" directly channeling the era's sonic palette. The band also incorporated guest harsh vocals from Einar Solberg of Leprous on the epic "The Architect," adding further diversity to their signature style.

Within Haken's discography, Affinity represents a deliberate stylistic shift from the 1970s influences of their previous album, The Mountain, to a more synth-driven, 1980s-oriented approach. The album was praised for its ambitious songwriting, technical proficiency, and seamless fusion of vintage and contemporary sounds. Critics highlighted its ability to balance nostalgic references with fresh, inventive compositions, cementing Haken's reputation as leading innovators in progressive rock and metal. Affinity received strong reviews upon release and further solidified the band's standing in the genre.
